thread.title: UPDATE: Qualcomm earnings show weak forecast amid massive fines, tax charge

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Qualcomm earnings show weak forecast amid massive fines, tax charge
text:
By Wallace Witkowski, MarketWatch
Tax law change, fines sock Qualcomm with $6 billion quarterly loss
Qualcomm Inc. managed to beat expectations with its earnings Wednesday, but the chip maker's outlook came up short and caused some concerns about Apple Inc.'s iPhone sales.
Qualcomm (QCOM) shares shifted between slight gains and losses in after hours trading following the release of the report. Shares closed the regular session Wednesday up 1.9% and are up 6.6% for the year. In comparison, the PHLX Semiconductor Index is up 8.7% and the S&P 500 index is up 5.6% this year.
The company reported a fiscal first-quarter net loss of $5.95 billion, or $4.03 a share, compared with net income of $682 million, or 46 cents a share, in the year-ago period. The recent quarter's results included a $6 billion charge from the recently passed U.S. tax law, $1.2 billion fine from the European Commission, $868 million Korea Fair Trade Commission fine and $778 million Taiwan Fair Trade Commission fine.
Don't miss: Tax bill lowered corporate tax rate, so why are some companies announcing charges? (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tax-bill-lowered-corporate-tax-rate-so-why-are-some-companies-announcing-charges-2018-01-18)
Adjusted earnings, which stripped out all those charges, were 98 cents a share. Of 18 analysts surveyed by FactSet, Qualcomm on average was expected to post adjusted earnings of 91 cents a share, after Qualcomm forecast adjusted profit of 85 cents to 95 cents a share.
Revenue rose to $6.07 billion from $6 billion in the year-ago period. Wall Street had expected revenue of $5.92 billion from Qualcomm, according to 14 analysts polled by FactSet. Qualcomm had predicted revenue of $5.5 billion to $6.3 billion.
For the fiscal second quarter, however, Qualcomm's estimates fell short of Wall Street's. The company forecast adjusted earnings of 65 cents to 75 cents a share on revenue of $4.8 billion to $5.6 billion. Analysts expected earnings of 86 cents a share on revenue of $5.58 billion heading into the report.
One of the factors that could have effected Qualcomm's forecast was an unexpected decline in modem orders from a major customer. Some observers took that note to be in reference to Apple Inc. (AAPL) , and shares in the iPhone maker declined in late trading (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-declines-in-late-trading-on-iphone-supplier-concerns-2018-01-31). Apple is scheduled to report earnings Thursday.
Apple earnings: Forget taxes and batteries, the $1,000 iPhone X remains the story (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-forget-taxes-and-batteries-the-1000-iphone-x-remains-the-story-2018-01-26)
Separately, Qualcomm said it and Apple rival Samsung Electronics Co.(005930.SE) expanded their strategic relationship "in various technology areas and across a range of mobile devices" through the transition to the 5G standard.
-Wallace Witkowski;
01-31-18 2112ET
